observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a compression-testing setup: a polished steel cylindrical platen sits above a yellow-and-black diagonally striped base, with a reddish-brown sample between them that is already split into several vertical slivers. Gray crushed powder coats the top and bottom contact zones. The background (cream wall with an arched recess, and a gray column with a yellow-black striped measuring rod on the right) stays fixed, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The steel platen moves downward gradually across the segment relative to the background.

The outermost left sliver, initially leaning slightly left, progressively rotates outward—its top edge shifts left and lower frame by frame—until it topples and exits the view at the bottom-left by the final frames.
A small fragment on the right side detaches and falls (seen as motion blur near the right edge in the middle of the segment).
The central and right main slivers remain standing, with the vertical crack between them staying open and largely unchanged in width.
The pile of gray debris on the base and the crushed zone under the platen persist with only minor settling.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fracture that produced the slivers is not shown; the sample is already broken at t=0.
Whether the platen began descending before this segment or continues/stops after the last frame is not visible.
The final resting position of the fallen left and right fragments is outside the crop.
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the sample (brick, concrete, or similar) is not confirmable.
Whether the left sliver's outward rotation is driven by the platen's descent or by loss of lateral support cannot be determined from the images alone.
The magnitude of platen travel is small and partly within frame-to-frame noise.
